newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BENGALS FIRE DAVID SHULA, NAME COSLET COACH.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BENGALS FIRE DAVID SHULA, NAME COSLET COACH.

text.p: The Cincinnati Bengals fired David Shula as head coach on Monday and named offensive coordinator Bruce Coslet as his replacement.

The firing came one day after the Bengals squandered a 21-0 lead in a 28-21 loss at San Francisco. Last week Bengals president and general manager Mike Brown said that the team was evaluating the head coach on a game-to-game basis.

"We all play a part in the responsibility, yet he's the one that has to face up to it," said Brown at a morning news conference. "There's a certain unfairness to it. He's done a good job. He deserved better results."
The Bengals are in last place in the AFC Central with a 1-6 record this season.
Shula, the son of legendary former coach Don Shula, had a 19-52 record in five seasons with Cincinnati.
"I think it was evident by the way the team played Sunday (at San Francisco) that we would get this thing turned around," said Shula, who was present at the news conference.
"I wish I was back in there looking at film getting ready for this week. But it's all about record and the results were not adequate."
The 37-year-old Shula, the youngest coach in the NFL, was in the final year of a five-year contract. He was named Bengals head coach in December 1991 at the age of 32.
Coslet, 50, was named Bengals offensive coordinator before the 1994 season and is widely credited for the development of quarterback Jeff Blake, who led the AFC with 28 touchdown passes last season.
Coslet's schemes also helped the emergence of receiver Carl Pickens, who set club records with 99 catches and 17 touchdowns in 1995.
"It's easy to say what you plan to do, words are meaningless," said Coslet. "But we'll work to turn it around and that starts with me."
It will be the second head coaching job for Coslet, who directed the New York Jets from 1990 to 1993. He compiled a 26-38 record as head coach and led the Jets to the playoffs in 1991.
Coslet, a former tight end, played eight years for the Bengals from 1969 to 1976.
